text: He quickly prepared a new fire. <break time="0.8s" /> In the open. <break time="0.8s" /> But his fingers were so numb. <break time="0.8s" /> That he could hardly hold the matches. <break time="0.8s" /> At last he held the whole bunch. <break time="0.8s" /> Between the heels of his hands. <break time="0.8s" /> And lit all seventy matches at once. <break time="0.8s" /> He held the blaze. <break time="0.8s" /> To the birch bark. <break time="0.8s" /> And it was only the smell, not any pain. <break time="0.8s" /> That told him his hands were burning. <break time="0.8s" /> But a piece of green moss fell. <break time="0.8s" /> On the tiny flame. <break time="0.8s" /> And when he tried to push it away. <break time="0.8s" /> The fire scattered and died. <break time="0.8s" /> Then a desperate idea came to him. <break time="0.8s" /> To kill the dog. <break time="0.8s" /> And warm his hands inside its body. <break time="0.8s" /> Until the feeling returned. <break time="0.8s" /> He called the dog. <break time="0.8s" /> But it heard a strange note of fear. <break time="0.8s" /> In his voice. <break time="0.8s" /> And would not come near him. <break time="0.8s" /> When it finally came close. <break time="0.8s" /> He caught it in his arms. <break time="0.8s" /> But his hands could neither hold a knife. <break time="0.8s" /> Nor grip the dog. <break time="0.8s" /> Then fear took hold of him. <break time="0.8s" /> And he ran blindly up the creek. <break time="0.8s" /> Toward the camp. <break time="0.8s" /> With the dog running at his heels. <break time="0.8s" /> He could not feel his feet strike the ground. <break time="0.8s" /> And it seemed to him. <break time="0.8s" /> That he was flying above the earth. <break time="0.8s" /> Perhaps, he thought. <break time="0.8s" /> If he ran far enough. <break time="0.8s" /> He would reach the camp. <break time="0.8s" /> And the boys would take care of him.
